title: Proposed therapy, developed in a Pcdh15-deficient mouse, for progressive loss of vision in human Usher syndrome
abstract: Usher syndrome type I (USH1) is characterized by deafness, vestibular areflexia, and progressive retinal degeneration. The protein-truncating p.Arg245* founder variant of PCDH15 (USH1F) has an ~2% carrier frequency amongst Ashkenazi Jews accounts for ~60% of their USH1 cases. Here, longitudinal phenotyping in 13 USH1F individuals revealed progressive retinal degeneration, leading to severe vision loss with macular atrophy by the sixth decade. Half of the affected individuals were legally blind by their mid-50s. The mouse Pcdh15 variant is equivalent to human p.Arg245*. Homozygous R250X Pcdh15 mice also have visual deficits and aberrant light-dependent translocation of the phototransduction cascade proteins, arrestin, and transducin. Retinal pigment epithelium (RPE)-specific retinoid cycle proteins, RPE65 and CRALBP, were also reduced in R250X Pcdh15 mice, indicating a dual role for protocadherin-15 in photoreceptors and RPE. Exogenous 9- R250X cis retinal improved ERG amplitudes in Pcdh15 mice, suggesting a basis for a clinical trial of FDA-approved retinoids to preserve vision in USH1F patients. R250X
